support_evidence_summary: The evidence confirms that Hurricane Patricia (2015) grew from a tropical storm to Category 5 in 24 hours, and that Typhoon Nora (1973) had its pressure record surpassed by one hurricane (which is Patricia, as indicated by Patricia being more intense).

state_snapshot.K_t:
Evidence:
[1] Originating from an area of low pressure over the western Pacific, Nora was first identified as a tropical depression on October 2, 1973.
[2] The ninth tropical storm and seventh hurricane and major hurricane of the season, Hattie originated from an area of low pressure that strengthened into a tropical storm over the southwestern Caribbean Sea on October 27.
[3] Originating from a sprawling disturbance near the Gulf of Tehuantepec, south of Mexico, in mid-October 2015, Patricia was first classified a tropical depression on October 20.
[4] After turning northwestward, the typhoon underwent a period of rapid intensification, during which its central pressure decreased by 77 mb (hPa; 2.27 inHg) in 24 hours.

Notes:
[bridge] Typhoon Nora in the raw evidence is from 1973, not 2015, indicating the question likely refers to a different storm.
